subject: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan
body:
From: Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Hi Priya,

We’re ready to proceed with the rollout_policy v2 schema + migration layer for Hosted canary GA (ENG-8421). Requesting your approval to move forward with the plan below (and start staging rollout this week).

Summary:
- Introduce rollout_policy v2 schema (versioned), with explicit baseline/candidate variants + percentage schedule + guardrails.
- Backward-compatible reads: accept existing beta policy shape, translate into v2 in-memory representation.
- Write path: GA workflows will write v2 only. Beta UI/users continue to function (read translation) until we announce sunset.
- Storage: persist v2 as canonical; keep beta fields read-only (no new writes) once flag is flipped.
- Migration: no hard backfill required for GA. We can opportunistically “normalize” existing beta policies on next edit, with a background task later if needed.

Open point we want sign-off on: propagation behavior across regions. We plan to rely on monotonic policy versioning and eventual convergence, but we want to ensure we’re not creating a customer-visible “split brain” where region A has weights X and region B has weights Y for too long.

Attaching:
- rollout_policy_v2_migration_plan_v3.docx
- adr-037-percentage-rollout-policy-schema.pdf

If you want, Ethan/Jordan and I can do a 15-min walk-through.

Thanks,
Benji

—
Benji Okafor
Platform Control Plane Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Thanks Benji.

Before I approve: I need crisp answers on multi-region staleness.

Two concrete concerns:
1) If a customer edits weights (e.g., 5% → 25% candidate), what’s our worst-case time where some regions still serve the old weights?
2) What happens if the Console “preview effective routing” calls into a control plane that is ahead of one region’s data plane? (We can’t show 25% and actually serve 5% for an extended window.)

I’m okay with eventual consistency, but we need:
- bounded staleness targets (SLO) and alerting
- deterministic evaluation (same inputs → same variant choice) given the same policy version
- a plan for when propagation is delayed (pause/rollback semantics must be safe)

Looping in SRE/Security if needed.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Engineering Sponsor, Platform
Redwood Inference



From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 11:21 AM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Priya,

Good questions. Here’s how we’re thinking about it today:

- Policy versions: each write produces an incrementing, monotonic version (per route policy object). Version is included in the routing payload.
- Data plane cache: routing nodes poll and cache policy snapshots. We’re also adding “min version” checks so a node won’t regress to an older snapshot.
- Worst-case staleness (today): depends on region polling interval + propagation lag. Target: p99 under 60s. Current observed in prod for similar configs is usually <10s, but we haven’t had a formal SLO.
- Preview endpoint: returns (policy_version, resolved weights) and will expose a “propagation status” indicator (e.g., last_seen_version per region). UI can show “still propagating” rather than implying it’s fully live.

We should tighten this with SRE: define control-plane propagation SLO and page when we exceed bounds.

I’ll let Jordan chime in on deterministic evaluation. Benji has the detailed migration mechanics.

Ethan

—
Ethan Park
Control Plane Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 12:07 PM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Adding on deterministic evaluation:

- Policy evaluation is purely functional: given (route_id, request metadata, policy_version, policy_body) we compute a variant decision.
- The weighted split is either:
  a) random per-request (default), or
  b) request-hash stickiness (explicitly configured).

For GA, we will pin the decision per streaming request at start of stream and reuse on retries (so we don’t mix variants within a session). That’s in the routing integration spec, but the policy schema supports it via “selection_strategy”.

Re staleness: determinism is with respect to a given version. If a region is behind (older version), it will deterministically choose based on that older version, but yes you get cross-region divergence until converged.

Proposal (to make this safe):
- Expose version in response headers for internal debug (and maybe customer-visible in Console only).
- Require guardrails before allowing >X% candidate, and allow “pause” to force baseline (0% candidate) which is safe even if some regions lag (because the policy change is monotonic and eventually arrives).

Jordan

—
Jordan Lee
Policy Engine Owner
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Oct 7, 2024 at 2:34 PM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Priya,

Agree we need a bounded staleness target before we call this GA-ready.

From SRE side, two failure modes we’ve seen historically:
1) “one region stuck” due to propagation race / cache not refreshing
2) “partial rollout of config” where control plane says it’s updated but data plane still serving the old policy for minutes

I’m fine with approving the migration as long as:
- We define and enforce an SLO for “policy propagation staleness” (e.g., p99 < 60s, p99.9 < 5m) and have alerts.
- There is a way to verify effective version per region during an incident.
- We have a clear rollback mechanism that does not depend on the stuck region being healthy.

Allison is drafting the SLO doc + alert thresholds. If the team commits to instrumenting per-region version lag, that addresses most of my concerns.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 8, 2024 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Priya,

Draft SLO proposal attached (hosted-rollout-control-plane-slos_draft.md). Highlights:

SLI: rollout_policy_propagation_staleness_seconds
- Defined as: (now - policy_last_applied_at_in_region) for the latest policy_version written for a given route.
- Reported per region, aggregated across routes with cardinality controls.

Targets:
- p99 < 60s during business hours
- p99.9 < 300s (5m)

Alerts:
- Ticket alert when p99.9 > 300s for 10m
- Page when p99.9 > 600s for 10m OR any region has “no apply” for >15m

Operational requirement:
- “Propagation status” endpoint returns last_seen_version per region (for internal tools + Console)

If we instrument this alongside the v2 migration, SRE is comfortable.

Allison

—
Allison Grant
Observability / SLOs
Redwood Inference



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 8, 2024 at 1:02 PM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Priya,

No security blocker from me on the migration mechanics.

One request: please ensure the policy version is included in audit events for create/update/pause/rollback so compliance teams can correlate “what changed” with “what was served” when troubleshooting (without logging request payloads).

Also: for the beta compatibility translation, make sure we don’t inadvertently accept ambiguous legacy fields (e.g., missing guardrails but high percentages). If the old schema can represent unsafe states, the translator should either:
- map to safe defaults, or
- reject writes / force edit to add guardrails before allowing escalation.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 9, 2024 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Policy schema migration approval: rollout_policy v2 + beta compatibility plan

Approved to proceed with rollout_policy v2 schema + migration layer, with the following conditions:

1) Staleness/SLOs
- Adopt Allison’s propagation staleness SLO and wire up the per-region version lag instrumentation + alerts before broad beta.
- Console preview must surface propagation state (don’t imply global state is live if one region is behind).

2) Monotonicity + regression protection
- Enforce monotonic version checks end-to-end so regions cannot apply older versions after observing newer ones.

3) Safe compatibility behavior
- Backward-compatible reads are fine.
- Any path that results in effectively unsafe settings (e.g., high candidate percentage without guardrails) should be blocked or coerced into safe defaults. I want this explicit in validation.

4) Auditability
- Ensure audit events include policy_version and a before/after diff of the policy object (Marcus’ point).

5) Rollout plan
- Keep behind feature flag in prod until we’ve validated staleness SLOs in staging + dogfood.

Please reply with an updated checklist on what lands in ENG-8421 vs follow-on tickets (ENG-8425 etc.).

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Engineering Sponsor, Platform
Redwood Inference
